question: Two capacitors of capacitances $3.0\ \mu\text{F}$ and $6.0\ \mu\text{F}$ are connected in parallel across a cell of emf $12\text{ V}$ and internal resistance $1.0\ \Omega$. (i) Find the equivalent capacitance and the total charge stored after the capacitors are fully charged. (ii) State the steady current through the cell after charging is complete and explain the role of internal resistance in this final condition.

options.A:
(i) $C_{\text{eq}}=18\ \mu\text{F}$ and $Q=2.16\times10^{-4}\text{ C}$.
(ii) The steady current is $12\text{ A}$ and internal resistance continuously reduces the capacitor voltage.
options.B:
(i) $C_{\text{eq}}=3.0+6.0=9.0\ \mu\text{F}$. After full charging, $V=\varepsilon=12\text{ V}$, so $Q=C_{\text{eq}}V=9.0\times10^{-6}\times12=1.08\times10^{-4}\text{ C}$.
(ii) The steady current is zero. Since $I=0$, there is no drop $Ir$ across the internal resistance, so the final capacitor voltage equals the emf.
options.C:
(i) $C_{\text{eq}}=2.0\ \mu\text{F}$ and $Q=2.4\times10^{-5}\text{ C}$.
(ii) The steady current is $1.0\text{ A}$ because capacitors always conduct DC.
options.D:
(i) $C_{\text{eq}}=9.0\ \mu\text{F}$ and $Q=9.0\times10^{-6}\text{ C}$.
(ii) Internal resistance causes a final voltage drop of $12\text{ V}$, making the capacitor voltage zero.
